title: Rabbi Bisna
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as a fourth-generation Amora of the Land of Israel. He reports R’ Layya (Eliaya) in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2:6; Hyman says it SHOULD READ likewise at the beginning of Moed Katan, where Layya’s name is missing. Tanchuma, Shemini 12, has him reporting R’ Chiyya (bar Abba); Yevamot 3:10 and Devarim Rabbah 4:6 have him reporting R’ Acha. At the end of Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 4:3 [end of halakhah 4 in the supplied transcription], Hyman gives the chain “Rabbi Bisna, Chanun bar Ba, in Rav’s name.” Shabbat 4:2 has him reporting R’ Yose son of R’ Chanina. Hyman lists as his colleagues R’ Avin, who disputes with him in Yevamot 3:9 and 3:10, and R’ Berekhya, who objects at the end of Maasrot, chapter 5, followed by R’ Bisna’s reply.

notes.text: Hyman says that Layya’s name is missing in the other passage, not that it should be removed. The compressed Bisna / Chanun bar Ba transmission chain is retained as a source question, without creating a compound personal name.

The whole saved Venice Pesachim4 scalar[2][6], under halakhah3, explicitly has full Rabbi Bisna, Chanin bar Ba in full Rav’s name. This supports the local Bisna title, not a compound Bisna-Chanun name or a silently supplied transmission connector. Hyman’s Chanun and end-of-halakhah4 remain beside the matching Chanin/4:3. Layya is said to be MISSING at the beginning of MoedKatan, not ordered removed; Hyman says it SHOULD READ as in Shabbat. His generation and colleagues are his classification, not a new chronology admission. Other abbreviated names remain R-prime; full Rav remains.

Hyman’s print (vol. I, p. 267) cites the end of halakhah 3 in Pesachim chapter 4, where the supplied transcription says 4. The consulted Venice and Guggenheimer texts have Chanin bar Ba where Hyman has Chanun, and leave the relation between Bisna and Chanin implicit. Shabbat 2:6 names Layya. In the consulted Moed Katan 1:1, Bisna reports the teaching in the name of R. La, a shorter form than Hyman’s proposed Layya. Tanchuma’s consulted Shmini 8:2 names Chiyya without the patronymic. Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 3:9 gives different explanations by Bisna and Avin (Avun in the witness), while 3:10 puts their names together before “in R. Acha’s name.” Maasrot 5:3 has Berekhya’s objection followed by R. Bisina’s answer. Hyman’s generation and teacher identifications remain his account.
